Three tools that write to your Garmin account did not do what they said. Two
could never work at all, and one quietly created the wrong thing. No tool was
added or removed — the server still declares 109.

These were found by actually running the writing tools against a real account,
rather than only the ones that read. Everything created during that testing was
deleted afterwards.

## Deleting a weigh-in never worked

`delete_weigh_in` asked the weight service to remove a measurement by its id
alone. That address answers "not found" for every id there is, so the call
always failed and the weigh-in always stayed. The service deletes by date and
version instead, which is what the tool now does.

The date is worked out from the weigh-in id, which encodes the day it was
recorded. If you logged a weight for a day other than the day you entered it,
pass that day explicitly:

```
delete_weigh_in(weighInId: "1787418037686", date: "2026-08-20")
```

## Deleting a blood pressure reading was impossible

`delete_blood_pressure` needs the reading's version number. The only tool that
could have supplied it, `get_blood_pressure`, was asking for day summaries
rather than the readings themselves — so the count of measurements came back
correct while the measurements list came back empty, and the version existed
nowhere you could reach it. You could see a reading and not delete it.

`get_blood_pressure` now returns the individual readings, each with its version.

## Workouts were created for the wrong sport

The workout service identifies a sport by number and ignores the name sent with
it. Six of the eight numbers were wrong, so a workout was quietly filed under a
different sport than the one asked for:

| You asked for | You got |
|---|---|
| swimming | strength training |
| strength | swimming |
| walking | HIIT |
| cardio | other |
| hiking | rejected |
| yoga | rejected |

Swimming and strength were each other's. The numbers have been rebuilt by asking
the service what it calls each one.

Asking for a sport the service does not have used to produce a **running**
workout without mentioning it — which is what happened to hiking. An unrecognised
sport is now refused by name, and the message lists what is available:

`running, cycling, other, swimming, strength, cardio, yoga, pilates, hiit, mobility, walking, rucking`

The workout taxonomy genuinely has no hiking. Use walking or rucking. It does
have pilates, HIIT, mobility and rucking, which were not reachable before.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.0...v4.5.1
